title: Kathy T NDE 3822
content: I was gravely ill and the doctors couldn't seem to find out what I was suffering from. I ended up in the intensive care unit, deteriorating quickly. Someone finally figured out what the illness was, and how to treat it, however, I was so weak by then I couldn't breathe on my own. I remember the week or so leading up to being transferred to the intensive care unit, but not actually being moved there. I do remember my doctor, seemingly waking me from a fog, to ask my permission to be placed on a respirator, as he knew I was against it. He pleaded with me to agree to one week. He was sure I would only need it for that long. I don't remember being taken for the procedure or how soon they did it. The next I knew, I was up in the corner of the room, where the walls and the ceiling join. I could see myself, lying in the bed. I don't recall seeing a respirator, just the room and me lying on the bed. No one else was there. I looked for a moment, and then looked directly across the room to the opposite corner. I then floated (more propelled) diagonally across the room into the opposite corner and entered the corner. When I came out on the other side, it opened up into a tunnel. Something like you'd see in a movie where people are in a spacecraft. It was a soft, luminous light, definitely tunnel like. I was propelling rather slowly, when I felt like someone had just wrapped a comforter, fresh from the dryer warm, around me. I then felt so warm and relaxed, like I was literally lounging in someone's very large hands. There are no words to accurately describe the feeling. Peace, contentment, and home - nothing comes close to being accurate. Anyway, I had the light, the warmth, the comfort and I was satisfied. This was okay and I began to pick up speed, propelling in the direction that was away from that corner I had entered. I then suddenly said 'No, I'm not ready to go yet', and threw out my arms to try to catch something on the walls of this tunnel of light to stop myself. Suddenly, my chest exploded in pain and all went black. It was days later when I was allowed to wake, that I was told I had pulled the respirator out. I discussed this event with my doctor, and we agreed that I was probably dying, and I pulled that respirator out as a way of shocking my body, or shocking myself back into by body. They could not believe, since I hadn't the strength to breathe on my own that I could have the strength to pull that respirator out. After I pulled it out, the doctors paralyzed me and induced a coma so I would rest. Apparently, I fought them every step of the way, and they decided they'd had enough. It was time for me to rest.

boundary_and_return.return_method_other_detail: Abrupt termination after she resisted going ('No, I'm not ready to go yet'), followed by 'my chest exploded in pain and all went black.'

stage_sequence.elements_other_detail: Intense warmth/comfort described as being wrapped in a warm comforter and 'lounging in someone's very large hands'; abrupt pain/blackout associated with return and later discovery she had pulled out the respirator.
stage_sequence.sequence_variation_description: OBE in room corner, then movement through corner into tunnel of soft luminous light; attempted to stop/declared not ready; pain/blackout; later awakened days later.

unique_elements.nonstandard_elements: Transition involved entering a room corner (where walls and ceiling join) to access the tunnel; later learned she had pulled out her respirator during the event.
unique_elements.notable_quotes: “The next I knew, I was up in the corner of the room, where the walls and the ceiling join.” / “It was a soft, luminous light, definitely tunnel like.” / “There are no words to accurately describe the feeling. Peace, contentment, and home - nothing comes close to being accurate.” / “No, I'm not ready to go yet.” / “Suddenly, my chest exploded in pain and all went black.”
